item.title: Shortage of dental treatment for children with additional needs in Kerry and Cork
item.description: There is a shortage of dental treatment available for children with additional needs in Kerry and Cork. Figures released to TD Colm Burke show there are funds for just nine senior public dentist roles offer this service across the two counties. These roles may also include treating older patients, people with mental health conditions and other vulnerable groups. item.title: 32 people are on trolleys at UHK today
item.description: 32 people were waiting on trolleys at University Hospital Kerry (UHK) this morning. That’s according to the INMO’s daily TrolleyWatch figures. 23 of the admitted patients, awaiting a bed, were on trolleys in the emergency ward, while nine were on trolleys elsewhere in the hospital. Advertisement Nationwide, there are 670 on trolleys, with University Hospital Galway being the most overcrowded with 81 inpatients waiting for a bed.

item.title: Proposals for masterplan for Tralee Sports Complex expected to be unveiled at end of month
item.description: Proposals for a masterplan for the Tralee Sports Complex are expected to be unveiled at the end of the month. On January 6th last year, part of the roof located over the sports hall, collapsed due to the weight of heavy snowfall. This happened early in the morning before the centre opened and no one was injured but significant damage was caused. item.title: New owners of historic South Kerry hotel say it’s vital the premises stayed open
item.description: The new owners of an historic South Kerry hotel say it’s important the business stayed open and its future is bright. Niall Moran was speaking after he and Bryan Marsal - who is one of the owners of Hogs Head golf club – bought the Butler Arms Hotel in Waterville. The 36-bedroom hotel went on the market last year, after previous owners – the Press Up hospitality group - went into receivership. item.title: MTU launches pilot green biorefinery at Kerry campus
item.description: Munster Technological University has launched a new pilot green biorefinery at its Kerry campus. The facility aims to reduce carbon footprint by developing technologies that convert grasslands into a circular bioeconomy. This includes the production of animal feeds, human-grade protein, prebiotics, flavours and bioenergy. item.title: Councillors in Killarney Municipal District (MD) have met to agree an updated settlements plan.
item.description: Councillors in Killarney Municipal District (MD) have met to agree an updated settlements plan. The plan designates or zones land for residential, commercial, recreational, and other uses, as well as defining policies for new building, infrastructure, and public spaces. The new settlements plan will replace the Killarney Town Development Plan, and the Killarney Municipal District Local Area Plan which lapsed in 2024. item.title: Bench warrant issued as gardaí believe Kerry stabbing accused has left Ireland
item.description: A bench warrant has been issued for a man accused of stabbing another man at an IPAS centre in Kerry. Gardaí told a sitting of Tralee District Court that they believe the man, who was previously granted bail, has fled the jurisdiction. The man cannot be named as he is an asylum seeker, and the identity of an international protection applicant is protected by the law in Ireland.
